Refund_not_showing_up: Customer already requested or was promised a refund from a merchant but cannot see it in their account or statement yet. Not asking how to obtain a refund (use request_refund).
activate_my_card: Customer asks how to activate a newly received card, whether it is activated, or reports that activation failed. Not linking an existing or found card to the app (use card_linking).
age_limit: Questions about the minimum age to open or use an account, or opening accounts for children or teenagers.
apple_pay_or_google_pay: Questions or problems using Apple Pay, Google Pay or Apple Watch, including topping up through them (e.g. an American Express card added to Apple Pay not working). Not general accepted card types (use supported_cards_and_currencies).
atm_support: Customer asks which ATMs or locations can be used to withdraw cash with the card, or where the nearest one is. Not about fees, declines or problems at the ATM.
automatic_top_up: Questions about the auto top-up feature: whether it exists, how to find or enable it, its rules and limits. Not general top-up limits (use top_up_limits).
balance_not_updated_after_bank_transfer: Customer transferred money into their own account (often from another bank, e.g. a UK account) and the balance has not updated or the funds have not appeared. Not money sent to someone else (use transfer_not_received_by_recipient).
balance_not_updated_after_cheque_or_cash: Customer deposited cash or a cheque and the money is not yet showing in their balance. Not asking whether or how cash/cheque can be used to top up (use top_up_by_cash_or_cheque).
beneficiary_not_allowed: An outgoing transfer is blocked because the beneficiary/recipient is not allowed or cannot be added, including failed attempts to buy or transfer cryptocurrency. Not a generic declined (declined_transfer) or failed (failed_transfer) transfer.
cancel_transfer: Customer wants to cancel, stop or reverse a transfer or transaction they made, typically sent by mistake or to the wrong account.
card_about_to_expire: Customer's card is expiring or has expired and they ask how to get a replacement, what it costs, how long it takes, or where it can be sent.
card_acceptance: Questions about where the card can be used or is accepted (shops, online, abroad). Not ATM locations (use atm_support) or countries where the service is offered (use country_support).
card_arrival: Customer ordered a card that has not arrived yet; asks where it is, how to track it, or what to do if it is late or lost in the post. Not general shipping times or options (use card_delivery_estimate).
card_delivery_estimate: Questions about how long card delivery takes in general, delivery to specific countries, express or chosen delivery dates. Not tracking an already-sent overdue card (use card_arrival).
card_linking: Customer wants to link or add an existing card in the app, or reactivate a card they cancelled as lost and then found. Not activating a brand new card (use activate_my_card).
card_not_working: General complaint that the physical card does not work at all for any transaction, without a specific declined payment. Not one declined payment (use declined_card_payment), contactless (contactless_not_working) or virtual card (virtual_card_not_working).
card_payment_fee_charged: Customer was charged an unexpected fee on a card payment/purchase or asks about card payment fees. Not ATM fees (cash_withdrawal_charge), transfer fees (transfer_fee_charged) or an unexplained small statement charge (extra_charge_on_statement).
card_payment_not_recognised: A card payment/purchase the customer did not make or does not recognise appears on the account. Not cash withdrawals (cash_withdrawal_not_recognised) or direct debits (direct_debit_payment_not_recognised).
card_payment_wrong_exchange_rate: A card purchase in a foreign currency was charged at a rate the customer thinks is wrong. Not ATM withdrawals abroad (use wrong_exchange_rate_for_cash_withdrawal) or general rate questions (use exchange_rate).
card_swallowed: The ATM kept, swallowed or did not return the customer's card; they ask how to get it back or what to do.
cash_withdrawal_charge: Customer was charged a fee for an ATM/cash withdrawal or asks about withdrawal fees. Not a wrong exchange rate on a foreign withdrawal (use wrong_exchange_rate_for_cash_withdrawal) or an unexplained statement charge (extra_charge_on_statement).
cash_withdrawal_not_recognised: A cash/ATM withdrawal the customer did not make appears on the account, often after a lost wallet or cloned card. Not unrecognised card purchases (card_payment_not_recognised).
change_pin: Customer wants to change or reset their PIN, including where (which ATMs, countries) it can be done. Not a PIN blocked by wrong attempts (pin_blocked) or locating the PIN of a new card (get_physical_card).
compromised_card: Customer suspects the card or its details have been compromised, stolen or used fraudulently and asks what to do or how to secure it. Not a physically lost card (lost_or_stolen_card).
contactless_not_working: Contactless payments are not working or the customer asks how to fix or set up contactless.
country_support: Questions about which countries the service operates in or whether residents of a country (e.g. EU, US) can get an account or card.
declined_card_payment: A card payment at a shop, online or for a subscription was declined; customer asks why. Not ATM withdrawals (declined_cash_withdrawal), transfers (declined_transfer), or a card that does not work at all (card_not_working).
declined_cash_withdrawal: An ATM cash withdrawal was declined or refused; customer asks why. Not a card swallowed by the ATM (card_swallowed) or receiving the wrong amount (wrong_amount_of_cash_received).
declined_transfer: An outgoing transfer was declined with a 'declined' message even though details look correct; customer asks why. Not beneficiary restrictions (beneficiary_not_allowed) or generic failures (failed_transfer).
direct_debit_payment_not_recognised: A direct debit the customer did not set up or does not recognise appears on the account; they want to dispute it. Not card purchases (card_payment_not_recognised).
disposable_card_limits: Questions about restrictions and limits of disposable virtual cards: how many can be created, number of transactions, where they can be used. Not how to obtain one (get_disposable_virtual_card).
edit_personal_details: Customer wants to change personal details such as name (e.g. after marriage), address after moving, or other account information.
exchange_charge: Questions about fees or commissions for currency exchange, and discounts for frequent exchanges. Not the exchange rate itself (exchange_rate) or how to exchange in the app (exchange_via_app).
exchange_rate: General questions about which exchange rates are used, how they are determined or what rate will apply. Not complaints about a wrong rate on a specific purchase or withdrawal.
exchange_via_app: Customer asks whether or how they can exchange money between currencies (e.g. GBP to AUD, USD to GBP) using the app. Not which currencies are supported in general (fiat_currency_support).
extra_charge_on_statement: Customer sees an unexplained extra charge on the statement, typically a small fixed amount like 1 pound, euro or dollar, sometimes pending. Not fees clearly tied to card payments, ATM withdrawals or transfers.
failed_transfer: An outgoing transfer failed, was unsuccessful or would not go through; customer asks why. Not explicitly 'declined' transfers (declined_transfer) or disallowed beneficiaries (beneficiary_not_allowed).
fiat_currency_support: Questions about which fiat currencies are supported for holding money and exchange, and whether multiple currencies can be held. Not cards/currencies accepted for topping up (supported_cards_and_currencies).
get_disposable_virtual_card: Customer asks how to get or order a disposable virtual card or what disposable cards are for. Not their limits (disposable_card_limits) or a standard virtual card (getting_virtual_card).
get_physical_card: Despite the name, customers ask where to find or how to get the PIN of their new physical card, or report the PIN has not arrived. Not changing a PIN (change_pin) or ordering a card (order_physical_card).
getting_spare_card: Customer wants an additional, second or spare physical card on the same account (e.g. for a family member) and asks about cost. Not the first physical card (order_physical_card) or a replacement for an expiring card.
getting_virtual_card: Customer asks how to get, order or find a (non-disposable) virtual card, or when it will be available. Not disposable virtual cards (get_disposable_virtual_card) or a virtual card that fails (virtual_card_not_working).
lost_or_stolen_card: Customer has lost their card or had it stolen and wants to block/freeze it or get a new one. Not suspected fraud with the card still in hand (compromised_card) or a lost phone (lost_or_stolen_phone).
lost_or_stolen_phone: Customer's phone with the app was lost or stolen; asks what to do, how to secure the account or use the card without the app.
order_physical_card: Customer asks how to order or get a physical card (e.g. having only a virtual one), its cost and delivery locations. Not an extra card (getting_spare_card) or tracking a sent card (card_arrival).
passcode_forgotten: Customer forgot or cannot use the app passcode/password to log in and wants to reset it. Not the card PIN (change_pin, pin_blocked).
pending_card_payment: A card payment/purchase still shows as pending or has not cleared; customer asks why or how long it takes. Not pending ATM withdrawals (pending_cash_withdrawal) or transfers (pending_transfer).
pending_cash_withdrawal: An ATM cash withdrawal still shows as pending, either after receiving the cash or after the ATM declined; customer asks why or how long. Not withdrawal fees or wrong amounts.
pending_top_up: A top-up is still pending or not yet completed; customer asks why or how long it takes. Not a top-up that failed (top_up_failed) or was reversed after appearing (top_up_reverted).
pending_transfer: An outgoing transfer is still in pending status; customer asks why it is not completed or how long pending lasts. Not a completed transfer the recipient did not get (transfer_not_received_by_recipient).
pin_blocked: Customer's PIN is blocked after too many wrong attempts and they want to unblock it. Not voluntarily changing the PIN (change_pin).
receiving_money: Questions about how others (friends, employers) can send money to the customer, including receiving salary, possibly in another currency. Not the customer moving their own money in (transfer_into_account).
request_refund: Customer wants to get a refund or cancel a purchase, or asks about refund/return policy. Not an already-requested refund that has not appeared (Refund_not_showing_up).
reverted_card_payment?: A card payment was reversed/cancelled and the money returned to the account, often with the seller saying they were not paid; customer asks why. Not reverted top-ups (top_up_reverted).
supported_cards_and_currencies: Questions about which card types (e.g. American Express, US credit cards) and currencies can be used to add money to the account. Not Apple/Google Pay (apple_pay_or_google_pay) or Visa vs Mastercard issued (visa_or_mastercard).
terminate_account: Customer wants to close, delete or terminate their account, often expressing dissatisfaction.
top_up_by_bank_transfer_charge: Questions about fees for topping up or receiving money via bank transfer, including SEPA and SWIFT transfers. Not fees for card top-ups (top_up_by_card_charge).
top_up_by_card_charge: Questions about fees for topping up with a card, e.g. European, US or international cards. Not bank transfer top-up fees (top_up_by_bank_transfer_charge).
top_up_by_cash_or_cheque: Customer asks whether or how they can top up with cash or a cheque. Not a deposit already made that is not showing (balance_not_updated_after_cheque_or_cash_deposit).
top_up_failed: A top-up attempt failed, was declined or did not work; customer asks why. Not a top-up that went through and was later reversed (top_up_reverted) or is still pending (pending_top_up).
top_up_limits: Questions about the maximum amount or frequency of top-ups. Not auto top-up settings (automatic_top_up).
top_up_reverted: A top-up appeared but was then cancelled or reversed and the money vanished, including failed crypto top-ups; customer asks why. Not a top-up that never went through (top_up_failed).
topping_up_by_card: Customer asks how to top up using a card, or whether others can top up their account; also reports a card top-up not showing in their balance. Not card top-up fees (top_up_by_card_charge).
transaction_charged_twice: Customer was charged twice or more for the same transaction or purchase and wants the duplicate removed.
transfer_fee_charged: Customer was charged a fee on a transfer, or the recipient received less than sent; asks why or whether transfers cost money. Not card payment fees (card_payment_fee_charged).
transfer_into_account: Customer asks how to transfer money into their account from another bank account or use a bank transfer to top up. Not top-up fees (top_up_by_bank_transfer_charge) or money from others (receiving_money).
transfer_not_received_by_recipient: Customer sent money to someone else, but the recipient says it has not arrived; asks where it is or how long it takes. Not incoming transfers to the customer's own account (balance_not_updated_after_bank_transfer).
transfer_timing: General questions about how long transfers take to arrive in the customer's account, often from specific regions (Europe, US, China). Not a specific transfer already overdue (balance_not_updated_after_bank_transfer).
unable_to_verify_identity: Customer is trying to verify their identity but it fails, is not accepted or is taking too long. Not how to verify (verify_my_identity) or why it is required (why_verify_identity).
verify_my_identity: Customer asks how to complete identity verification, where to do it, or which documents are needed. Not a failing verification (unable_to_verify_identity).
verify_source_of_funds: Customer asks about verifying or proving the source of their funds, or where their money comes from.
verify_top_up: Questions about verifying a top-up or top-up card, where to find the verification code, and why verification is needed.
virtual_card_not_working: Customer's virtual or disposable virtual card does not work or was rejected for a payment. Not the physical card (card_not_working).
visa_or_mastercard: Questions about whether the issued card is Visa or Mastercard and whether the customer can choose or get one or both.
why_verify_identity: Customer asks why identity verification is required, objects to it, or asks whether they can use the account without it. Not how to verify (verify_my_identity).
wrong_amount_of_cash_received: The ATM dispensed a different amount of cash than requested or than debited in the app. Not a wrong exchange rate on a foreign withdrawal (wrong_exchange_rate_for_cash_withdrawal).
wrong_exchange_rate_for_cash_withdrawal: Customer thinks the exchange rate (or resulting cost) on a foreign-currency ATM withdrawal was wrong or too high, or asks about rates for cash withdrawals abroad. Not card purchases (card_payment_wrong_exchange_rate).
